UnitStatement: This document is the authoritative specification for Chirality App physical structures, file formats, schemas, runtime mechanics, session storage, validation surfaces, and layout conventions.
Normative keywords MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are used in their ordinary specification sense.
The instruction root is the release-managed resource set bundled with the desktop app or supplied through CHIRALITY_INSTRUCTION_ROOT during development.

A complete source tree or packaged app instruction root requires entries including AGENTS.md, README.md, agents/, docs/, docs/DIRECTIVE.md, docs/CONTRACT.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/TYPES.md, and docs/PLAN.md.
docs/WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT.md and PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md are required instruction-root entries where required by packaging/integrity policy.
The instruction root is read-only during ordinary project execution.
Writes to the instruction root MUST be blocked by runtime hooks and path policy.
Packaged builds MUST verify instruction-root integrity.
Missing required instruction-root assets are a P0 packaging and runtime-readiness blocker.
The working root (projectRoot) is the user-selected local project folder.
The working root MUST be an absolute existing directory.
The working root MUST be readable and writable by the app.
The working root MUST NOT be inside the instruction root.
The working root contains project execution state, deliverables, tool roots, sessions, and local artifacts.
The working root is the ordinary location where agents and tools write project truth.

Runtime configuration state such as UI presets, API keys, provider/SDK linkage, adapter transcript cross-references, session metadata, and window layout is non-authoritative convenience state unless imported into a governed project file.
An execution instance is rooted at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/ and contains package folders plus tool roots.

The execution root layout includes INIT.md, package folders PKG-XX_{PkgLabel}/, and tool-root folders such as _Aggregation/, _Change/, _Coordination/, _Decomposition/, _Estimates/, _Reconciliation/, _Archive/, _Scripts/, and _Sources/.
Package folders are named {PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)}/.
Package folders MUST include the 1_Working/ subfolder for active deliverables.
Package folders SHOULD include 0_References/ and 0_References/_Archive/ for package-level and archived references.
Package folders SHOULD include 1_Working/_Archive/, 2_Checking/ with From/ and To/, and 3_Issued/ with _Archive/.
Tool roots include _Aggregation/ for aggregation snapshots and templates and _Change/ for change-management records.
Tool roots include _Coordination/, _Decomposition/, _Estimates/, _Reconciliation/, _Archive/ for baseline snapshots with checksums, _Scripts/, and _Sources/.
Snapshot-producing workflows SHOULD write timestamped immutable folders and MAY update _LATEST.md pointer files.
Each deliverable occupies {EXECUTION_ROOT}/{PKG-ID}_{PkgLabel}/1_Working/{DEL-ID}_{DelLabel}/.

A deliverable MUST contain _STATUS.md (lifecycle state and history), _CONTEXT.md (identity, package, decomposition reference, traceability), _DEPENDENCIES.md (dependency summary and run history), and _REFERENCES.md (source references and hash notes).
A deliverable SHOULD contain _SEMANTIC.md for the PREPARATION baseline as a semantic placeholder or lens.
When initialized, a deliverable SHOULD contain Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
Dependencies.csv SHOULD be present when tracked as a structured dependency register v3.1.
MEMORY.md SHOULD be present as the canonical deliverable-local working memory.
_MEMORY.md MUST NOT exist in this project profile; it is a disabled noncanonical memory file.
The minimum PREPARATION fileset is _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _REFERENCES.md, and a _SEMANTIC.md placeholder.
The document kit consists of Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
_STATUS.md uses a defined markdown format with a status heading, Current State, Last Updated, and a History section.
The valid _STATUS.md state progression is OPEN -> INITIALIZED -> SEMANTIC_READY -> IN_PROGRESS -> CHECKING -> ISSUED.
State OPEN means the folder exists with the minimum viable fileset; INITIALIZED means draft documents or document kit initialized.
State SEMANTIC_READY means a semantic lens or placeholder is generated; IN_PROGRESS means human/agent work is underway.
State CHECKING means under human review; ISSUED means released/issued by a human.
Transition to OPEN is authorized by PREPARATION/scaffold; OPEN to INITIALIZED by 4_DOCUMENTS or human.
INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY is authorized by CHIRALITY_FRAMEWORK or human; INITIALIZED or SEMANTIC_READY to IN_PROGRESS by human or WORKING_ITEMS.
IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING and CHECKING to ISSUED are authorized by a human.
_STATUS.md is the canonical lifecycle file.
_STATUS.md transitions are forward-only unless a human explicitly amends the record.
Transitions to CHECKING or ISSUED require approval SHA evidence.
SDK/MCP status-transition tools MUST enforce the lifecycle transition rules.
_CONTEXT.md has a required structure including Name, Package, Discipline, Type, Responsible, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Anticipated Artifacts, Scope Traceability, and Decomposition Reference.
_CONTEXT.md header fields SHOULD match the accepted decomposition.
_CONTEXT.md is created by PREPARATION/scaffold and is human-maintained thereafter.

_DEPENDENCIES.md is a hybrid container with human-owned and agent/tool-owned sections: Dependency Tracking Mode, Declared Upstream, Declared Downstream, Extracted Dependency Register, Lifecycle Summary, Run Notes, and Run History.
Dependency tracking mode NOT_TRACKED means dependencies are coordinated externally by humans.
Dependency tracking mode DECLARED means human-declared upstream/downstream only.
Dependency tracking mode TRACKED means full extraction via dependency workflow and Dependencies.csv.
_REFERENCES.md has a required structure with Applicable References (RefName/ID, Location, Relevance, ContentHash) and Notes.
_REFERENCES.md ContentHash is a 64-char lowercase SHA-256, or TBD, or an ERROR with reason.
Reference paths SHOULD be relative where practical.
Out-of-folder references SHOULD include ContentHash when tooling is available.
Hash bypasses require human approval and durable bypass records.
MEMORY.md is the canonical deliverable-local working memory file organized by semantic topic then chronologically.
MEMORY.md sections include Key Decisions & Human Rulings, Domain Context, Open Items, Proposal History, and Interface & Dependency Notes.
_MEMORY.md MUST NOT be created in this project profile.
Every Dependencies.csv row MUST include RegisterSchemaVersion set to v3.1.
Dependencies.csv MUST include RegisterSchemaVersion (v3.1), DependencyID unique within the register, FromPackageID, FromDeliverableID, and FromDeliverableName.
DependencyClass MUST be ANCHOR or EXECUTION; Direction MUST be UPSTREAM or DOWNSTREAM.
AnchorType, DependencyType, and TargetType are MUST enum columns defined in TYPES.
Optional target columns include TargetPackageID, TargetDeliverableID, TargetRefID, and TargetLocation; TargetName SHOULD be a human-readable target.
EvidenceFile and SourceRef are conditionally required columns holding source filename and path-plus-heading, or 'location TBD'.
EvidenceQuote SHOULD be a short quote of no more than 30 words; Explicitness SHOULD be EXPLICIT or IMPLICIT.
SatisfactionStatus SHOULD record closure status; Confidence SHOULD be HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.
Origin MUST be DECLARED or EXTRACTED; FirstSeen and LastSeen MUST be ISO dates; Status MUST be ACTIVE or RETIRED.
Extension columns MAY be present and are non-breaking, including EstimateImpactClass and ConsumerHint.
DependencyID MUST be unique within a deliverable register.
FromDeliverableID MUST match the host deliverable ID.
ANCHOR rows use IMPLEMENTS_NODE or TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT with DependencyType=OTHER.
EXECUTION rows use AnchorType=NOT_APPLICABLE.
Dependency rows are retired, not deleted.
Legacy missing RegisterSchemaVersion is normalized on write to v3.1.
Agent instruction files use AGENT_*.md names.
Agent instruction files require a header with [[DOC:AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS]], an AGENT INSTRUCTIONS title, and AGENT_TYPE set to 0, 1, or 2.

The required Agent Type table includes AGENT_TYPE, AGENT_CLASS (PERSONA or TASK), INTERACTION_SURFACE (chat, INIT-TASK, spawned, or both), WRITE_SCOPE, BLOCKING (never or allowed), and PRIMARY_OUTPUTS.
Agent instruction files require section markers PROTOCOL, SPEC, STRUCTURE, and RATIONALE delimited by [[BEGIN:X]] and [[END:X]].
Agent instruction section precedence is PROTOCOL > SPEC > STRUCTURE > RATIONALE.
Machine-consumed YAML frontmatter MAY include description, subagents, tools, model, max_turns, disallowed_tools, and auto_approve_tools.
Runtime MUST treat UI visibility of an option as non-authoritative; governance and permission policy remain authoritative.
Legacy sessions may exist as {sessionRoot}/{sessionId}.json.
Current legacy session fields include sessionId, projectRoot, persona, mode, createdAt, updatedAt, engineSessionId, claudeSessionId, bootFingerprint, bootedAt, and model.
Legacy session records MUST remain readable during migration.
The canonical vNext session layout is .chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/ containing session.json, events.jsonl, turns/<turnId>.json, artifacts/, and sdk/.
CHIRALITY_SESSION_ROOT is an optional override for the session root.
session.json SHOULD include sessionId, projectRoot, persona, mode, createdAt, updatedAt, model, bootFingerprint, and engineSessionId.

session.json SHOULD include SDK linkage fields sdkSessionId, sdkProjectKey, sdkTranscriptPath or sdkSessionStoreKey, sdkConfigDir, sdkSettingSources, sdkPackageVersion, sdkClaudeCodeVersion, and sdkResumeMode.
events.jsonl is the product-owned Chirality audit mirror.
SDK transcripts are secondary runtime state unless imported into HarnessEvent form.
The product SHOULD prefer SDK transcript placement or mirroring under the working root or parent project-controlled folder using SessionStore, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or both when reliable.
If the SDK writes under ~/.claude/projects/..., Chirality MUST cross-reference the path or store key, keep events.jsonl canonical, and record residual risk in the reliance-boundary register.
HarnessEvent has fields schemaVersion (1), eventId, sessionId, optional turnId, optional parentEventId, timestamp, type, and data as a record.
JSONL writes MUST append newline-delimited events in write sequence.
Event IDs MUST be unique.
Secrets MUST NOT be stored in events.
Large payloads MUST be stored as artifacts and referenced by path.
Replay MUST ignore malformed trailing lines and surface diagnostics.
Event schema evolution MUST be backward-compatible or explicitly versioned.

Initial event categories include session.created, session.resumed, turn.accepted, turn.started, adapter.initialized, model.request.started, model.delta, model.completed, turn.completed, turn.failed, and turn.cancelled.

Later event categories include tool.queued, tool.permission, tool.started, tool.progress, tool.completed, tool.failed, hook.started, hook.completed, context.compacted, subagent.started, subagent.completed, and runtime.mirror.error.
Chirality MUST define an AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract separate from provider/SDK APIs.

The runtime engine's target responsibilities include accepting validated turn input, persisting turn.accepted before adapter/model execution, yielding browser UIEvents, and persisting canonical HarnessEvents.

The runtime engine's target responsibilities include enforcing or invoking permission decisions, exposing only permitted tools, linking adapter session metadata, handling interrupt/cancel behavior, and persisting terminal outcomes.
AgentEnginePort defines runTurn(input: TurnInput) returning AsyncIterable<UIEvent> and an optional interrupt(sessionId) returning Promise<void>.
TurnInput MUST include the active session, normalized project root, persona, mode, resolved runtime options, content blocks, attachment summaries, and cancellation signal where applicable.
Provider/SDK messages are not the browser contract and not the canonical persisted event contract.
Provider/SDK-specific names and IDs appear only as adapter metadata.
EngineAdapter MUST translate external message names, session IDs, tool names, permission modes, transcript paths, and hook names into Chirality-owned contracts.
Provider-specific values MAY be retained under explicit adapter metadata fields.
Any provider/SDK-backed adapter MUST pass engine conformance tests before production default use.
The current Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic adapter is the first concrete adapter and current shipped path.
A stub adapter remains available for deterministic tests.
/api/harness/turn remains a transport adapter that validates request shape, obtains session lock, forwards input to TurnEngine, writes SSE, and handles cleanup, and does not own runtime policy.
Turn streams emit named SSE events with JSON payloads: session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, and process:exit.
Existing SSE event names MUST remain compatible during SDK adoption.
Additional tool progress events MAY be introduced only with UI compatibility handling.
The stream MUST terminate with a process-level completion/error signal unless the client disconnects.
Client disconnect cleanup MUST record cancellation once the event log exists.

Chirality uses a provider-adapter runtime architecture with Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic as the first concrete adapter and current shipped path, subject to R0/R1 empirical verification and ongoing conformance tests.
Concrete non-Anthropic providers require bounded future implementation scope.
Shipped builds MUST use settingSources: [].
Development-only project settings MAY use ['project'] behind explicit environment configuration.
User and local setting sources MUST NOT be used in shipped builds.
API key precedence is UI safeStorage key first, then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Key material is supplied to the provider/SDK environment only as needed for active turns and redacted from logs/events.

Safe adapter runtime metadata SHOULD include provider/SDK package version, Claude Code subprocess version where knowable, provider/SDK permission mode, visible tool list, MCP server names, settings-source posture, provider/SDK session ID and resume mode, and transcript/store linkage.
Model fallback chain is opts.model -> CHIRALITY_GLOBAL_MODEL or instruction-root frontmatter -> runtime default.
Tools fallback chain is opts.tools -> persona frontmatter -> runtime default; max turns is opts.maxTurns -> persona frontmatter -> runtime default.
Mode fallback is request/session mode -> runtime default; persona fallback is request/session persona -> HELP_HUMAN or configured default.
Unknown option keys MUST be ignored with warnings rather than silently mutating behavior.

The persona composer builds the system prompt from the Chirality governance preface, selected agents/AGENT_<persona>.md content, working-root summary, mode policy, permitted tool surface, and professional-boundary reminders.

Boot fingerprints SHOULD include hashes for persona content, governance preface, mode, adapter tool names/versions, permission-policy version, settings-source posture, MCP server versions, and subagent policy version.
First-adapter SDK built-ins map to SDK names: Read for read file, LS/Glob for list files, Grep for search, Write for write file, Edit for edit file, and Bash for shell command.
Chirality-specific deterministic operations use mcp__chirality__* names.
Initial Chirality MCP tools include mcp__chirality__status_read (read _STATUS.md) and mcp__chirality__status_transition (apply authorized lifecycle transition with approval SHA, write-gated).
Initial Chirality MCP tools include mcp__chirality__deps_read (read and validate Dependencies.csv) and mcp__chirality__deps_write (append/update dependency rows preserving v3.1 schema, write-gated).
Initial Chirality MCP tools include mcp__chirality__scope_scan (bounded workspace scope scan, read) and mcp__chirality__scaffold (wrap scaffold service or dry-run preview, gated).
Unknown opts.tools names MUST produce structured validation errors.
Tool ordering MUST be deterministic.
Denied tools SHOULD be omitted from model context where possible.
allowedTools MUST NOT be treated as a restriction boundary by itself.
Explicit hard-deny precedence, disallowedTools, permissionMode, canUseTool, and hooks enforce restrictions.
Chirality readOnly mode prefers SDK plan or dontAsk with read tools pre-approved and denies write/edit/bash/network-capable and unexpected tools.
Chirality workspaceWrite mode uses SDK acceptEdits only after write hooks pass and enforces project-root containment, instruction-root block, symlink rejection, and provenance.
Chirality dontAsk mode uses SDK dontAsk or an equivalent deny-without-prompt overlay, pre-approving exact safe tools while everything else denies without prompting.
Chirality ask mode uses SDK default with canUseTool, presenting UI approval for governed writes/shell and persisting the decision before returning SDK allow/deny.
Chirality bypass mode uses SDK bypassPermissions only in developer-local mode and still applies hard-deny rules, disallowed tools, path hooks, instruction-root protection, and subagent governance.
Required hooks include path containment (deny filesystem operations outside the active project root) and instruction-root protection (deny writes under the instruction root).
Required hooks include symlink write rejection, write budget enforcement, and provenance append where policy requires.
Required hooks include PreCompact mirror (persist compaction boundary), Stop/finalization (persist terminal outcome), and subagent governance (gate the Agent tool through evaluateSubagentGovernance).
Hook failures fail closed for write, shell, domain, and subagent actions.
Supported attachment extensions are .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .pdf, .txt, .md, and .csv.

The server-side attachment resolver MUST enforce path validation, regular-file check, symlink rejection, extension allowlist, readability, a per-file 10 MB limit, and a total raw-byte 18 MB per-turn limit.
Partial attachment failure is non-fatal when executable content remains; if all attachments fail and user text is empty the request fails with ATTACHMENT_FAILURE.
The API key store uses Electron storage at app.getPath('userData')/credentials/api-key.enc.
API key store rules: use Electron safeStorage, do not write key material to working root, do not log key material, and do not persist key material in runtime events.
API key status may report source as ui, env, or none.
Renderer outbound traffic is allowlisted for loopback and the current shipped Anthropic API path.
Node/provider/SDK calls must not silently broaden network policy.
Provider-adapter generality is approved strategically, but concrete non-Anthropic providers, remote MCP, plugins, and network-capable tools require bounded governed future implementation scope.
Harness APIs include POST /api/harness/session/create (create session bound to projectRoot, persona, mode) and POST /api/harness/session/boot (boot session and persist boot metadata).
Harness APIs include GET /api/harness/session/list (list sessions for normalized project root) and GET/DELETE /api/harness/session/[id] (retrieve or delete session).
Harness APIs include POST /api/harness/turn (execute turn and stream UI events over SSE) and POST /api/harness/interrupt (interrupt active turn).
Harness APIs include POST /api/harness/scaffold (scaffold execution root from decomposition markdown).
Existing harness route shapes remain stable during adapter adoption and TurnEngine extraction.
Workspace APIs include POST /api/working-root/validate, GET /api/working-root/tree (bounded file tree), and GET /api/working-root/scope (scan deliverables and knowledge types).
Workspace APIs include GET /api/project/deliverables (deliverables plus knowledge decomposition metadata) and GET /api/working-root/deliverable/status (read _STATUS.md snapshot).
Workspace APIs include POST /api/working-root/deliverable/status/transition (apply allowed lifecycle transition) and GET/PUT /api/working-root/deliverable/dependencies (read/write Dependencies.csv).

Domain-engine endpoints and tools are provisional future platform interfaces that must not be implemented as current-release scope and must not imply automated professional acceptance or direct protected-model writes.

Candidate domain endpoint families include /api/domain/profiles/list, /api/domain/profiles/validate, /api/domain/artifacts/scan, /api/domain/operations/propose, /api/domain/operations/validate, and /api/domain/operations/apply.
Future domain profiles MUST define protected paths, proposal paths, operations, artifact types, deterministic adapter manifests, and boundary notices.
Applying a domain operation requires explicit human acceptance.
Required local checks from frontend/ are npm run test, npm run typecheck, npm run harness:validate:premerge, and npm run instruction-root:integrity.
Packaging uses npm run desktop:dist.
Expected packaging outputs are frontend/dist/Chirality-0.1.0-arm64.dmg, frontend/dist/mac-arm64/Chirality.app, and frontend/artifacts/harness/instruction-root-integrity/latest/summary.json.
Notes: frontend/ path references; known publish-time drift per project memory

UnitStatement: Section 8 validation verifies server reachable, session CRUD, boot error taxonomy, smoke stream ordering, session persistence and resume continuity, permissions behavior, interrupt behavior, and SDK-native stream handling with no legacy parser regressions.

Section 9 runtime validation IDs to add as phases land include section9.runtime_engine_contract, section9.adapter_turn_engine_event_log, section9.adapter_message_mapper, and section9.session_event_replay.

Section 9 runtime validation IDs include section9.reliance_boundary_register, section9.settingsources_isolation, section9.sdk_session_link_resume, and section9.permission_overlay_hard_deny_precedence.

Section 9 runtime validation IDs include section9.tool_runtime_read_file, section9.chirality_mcp_status_dependencies, section9.path_containment_hook, section9.instruction_root_protection_hook, section9.tool_result_budget, section9.context_compaction_boundary, section9.subagent_governance_hook, and section9.domain_profile_validation.
Manual macOS DMG release verification checks that the binary is arm64, LSMinimumSystemVersion is 15.0.0 or later, and signing posture is unsigned/adhoc as scoped.

Manual release verification checks that app resources contain required instruction-root assets, the working-root selector is available, and current loopback plus Anthropic network guardrails remain in force.

Manual release verification checks that a first-adapter SDK-backed turn can start in the packaged app after R1, the SDK subprocess/binary is executable from package layout, and SDK transcript storage/mirroring follows the accepted R1 decision.
Sanitize(name) replaces /, \, :, *, ?, double-quote, <, >, and | with a hyphen.
Sanitize(name) collapses consecutive whitespace to one space and trims leading/trailing whitespace.
Folder names are Package {PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)} and Deliverable {DEL-ID}_{Sanitize(DeliverableName)}.
Canonical unsanitized names are stored in _CONTEXT.md and decomposition records.
